audio.G: Team G combines Sheoldred Pox with Oloro enchantment control. The black deck attacks hands, lands, and life totals while the Esper deck uses mana rocks, enchantment recursion, and counterspells to preserve a winning board. Their most alarming line is Bloodletter followed by Pox: from sixty life, the opposing team can lose eighty while our team loses forty. Sorin offers another abrupt life-total conversion. Oloro supplies passive recovery, and Test of Endurance can win at the next upkeep without ever casting the commander. These are alternatives that require coordination: casting Pox at the wrong moment can destroy your own Test plan, and Contamination can strand your teammate's colored spells. Expect a turn spent establishing mana, then either a protected threshold win or disruptive black conversion. This team may be substantially more oppressive than its modest commander prices suggest, especially if repeated resource denial is acceptable.
audio.H: Team H pairs an Esper tempo and counterspell deck with Chulane creature combo. Tymna draws from combat, Malcolm makes Treasure from its own Pirates, and inexpensive evasive threats keep cards flowing while the team holds interaction. Chulane supplies the creature engine, supported by bounce creatures, Aluren, and redundant value loops. The sharpest two-player adaptation puts Acererak in the Esper deck: once the Bant player resolves Aluren, the teammate can repeatedly cast Acererak for free and drain both opposing heads through dungeon rooms. Neither commander is necessary for that line. The Esper deck also has its own Oracle and Consultation finish, so removing Chulane is insufficient. Aluren gives opponents the same creature permission, and removal, casting restrictions, and trigger suppression remain meaningful answers. This is an intentionally severe benchmark, with a possible third-turn team line rather than evidence of a measured win rate. The two-point Aluren package deserves urgent organizer review.
audio.I: Team I combines Gitrog land recursion with Shorikai Stoneblade control. Gitrog turns discarded or sacrificed lands into cards, finds Dark Depths, and rebuilds resources through Loam and graveyard recursion. Shorikai filters cards and produces equipment carriers while Stoneforge finds Batterskull or Kaldra; the blue-white deck also holds counterspells and has its own artifact-mana finish. The pairing deliberately avoids graveyard hate and creature shutdown effects that would disable Gitrog. Marit Lage is a substantial threat, but twenty damage is not an immediate kill against sixty shared life. For a more decisive route, the lands deck includes a fully specified Woodland and Analyst mana loop that works after removing its own Gitrog, avoiding mandatory draw exhaustion. Both heads can win independently, although graveyard hate pressures the lands player and artifact hate pressures Shorikai. This looks like a powerful benchmark with real setup costs, not proof that the budget has achieved balance.

# Batch3 team plans — season0-proposed

## G — Denial plus enchantment control
G1 establishes black mana, Sheoldred, discard and renewable fodder. G2 places colored rocks, finds Test/Felidar or assembles its own enchantment drain loop, and keeps stack interaction. G1 can convert Bloodletter+Pox, Sorin+Bloodletter, or Peer+Sheoldred into decisive life loss. G2 Wound Reflection can finish G1's Sorin or Pox without shared control. G2's own Exquisite/Bond/Tenacity and G1's own Blood/Vito packages are legitimate independent alternatives; splitting these life-event engines is not.

The lock plan is deliberately adversarial. Contamination/Ophiomancer can deny both enemies while Oloro gains life from the command zone. It also turns G2 lands into black-only sources: require its nonland colored rocks or a deployed win before committing. Bottomless Pit, Necrogen Mists, Liliana, Smallpox, Death Cloud and Pox cost G2 cards or permanents too. Deploy durable enchantments and rocks first, or choose the quick threshold plan instead. G2 Replenish recovers only its own enchantments. Pox is not a free asymmetrical wipe.

Against fast spell combo, use Duress/Thoughtseize on the more dangerous head and G2 Veto/ordinary counters on the stack. A single discard spell cannot clear two hands. Against creature decks, black edicts/Deluge and G2 Verdict trade cards but threaten your own engines. Graveyard hate attacks drain/reanimation but not an already-deployed Test. Opposing Drannith limits battlefield commanders but not Oloro's command-zone trigger. Life-total locks, counters, enchantment removal and attack pressure challenge Test. This pair is mana-hungry and has fewer free counters than H/I; no win percentages claimed.

## H — Two independent finishers plus global creature permission
H1's changelings/Pirates/evasive threats generate Malcolm Treasure, Tymna cards and combat pressure. H2's mana dorks develop Chulane, with Aluren, Earthcraft, Alarm, bounce creatures and creature tutors supplying overlapping engines. H1 can win through its own Oracle/Consultation; H2 can draw toward its own Lab Maniac; H1 Acererak plus H2 Aluren is a separate cross-controller win requiring neither commander. Chulane never draws for teammate casts.

Aluren is global: all four players may flash eligible creatures. Enemy Opposition Agent, Bowmasters, Faerie Mastermind and combo creatures may exploit that window. Tidal Barracuda is a separately paid4-mana way to suppress enemy casting during the friendly turn; it is not itself Aluren-eligible. Chant/Abeyance restrict one enemy, leaving the other to interact. Speaker/Earthcraft can explicitly target a teammate's land, while Curio and ordinary bounce engines refer to their own controller's permanents.

Countering Aluren, removing Acererak at the right time, Torpor Orb/Hushbringer, Rule of Law, Drannith and creature ability suppression attack different routes. A deployed Lab Maniac needs protection from removal before the final draw. Oracle's trigger is different and may beat simple creature removal. Do not cast H1 Oracle into a resolved hostile draw effect or an ETB suppressor. H1 deliberately omits anti-creature stax and global draw denial that would shut off H2. H1 keeps14-point Force despite the squeeze because protecting a team-wide win is its role. Evasive creatures do not guarantee hits through two defending boards.

## I — Lands plus Stoneblade control
I1 uses Dakmor outlets, Loam, sacrifice/recursion and land tutors for draw/mana. It has a fully specified non-random Woodland/Analyst/Spelunking/Resources loop after removing Gitrog, as well as draw-dependent Dakmor routes and Dark Depths pressure. I2 deploys Stoneforge threats and Shorikai Pilots while keeping blue interaction; Scepter/Reversal or Basalt/Rings plus Ballista gives an independent own-controller artifact route.

The choice of Shorikai is intentional: its actual tournament shells provide Azorius filtering, artifact mana and stack protection, while its Pilot bodies carry Equipment. It is eligible under current903.3 and remains free in the command zone. The Stoneblade package changes the source engine materially, so this exact hybrid is newly designed, not an attributed tournament winner.

Do not import source RIP/Cage/Totem/Humility just because they are strong Shorikai cards. They sabotage Gitrog. Lantern's enemy-only graveyard exile is appropriate. Opposing RIP/Endurance/Surgical can hurt I1; I2's independent non-graveyard artifact and Equipment routes remain useful. Artifact hate attacks I2 but not Loam/Depths. Combat blockers, edicts and exile answer Marit Lage/Kaldra; a20/20 is not a60-life kill. Sword untaps I2 lands only, and Equip cannot attach to I1's creatures. Never borrow I1 mana for I2's loop.

H dungeon accounting: using fully resolved Lost Mine rooms requires119 casts and29 Temple draws to reach30 Dark Pools. At60 enemy shared life, retain>=29 library cards and do not assume unlimited safe draws. This qualification does not remove theT3 example, but matters late in a long game.

# Attributed foundations and original adaptations

All twelve complete source registrations are frozen in research/foundations.json with raw snapshot checksums, event/player locators and exact card inventories. Standings are those of the source events, not these adaptations. Every head has two list foundations, but their empirical strength differs substantially.

G1: the archived Sheoldred pilots include a17/18 event entry and a24/40 entry, not demonstrated elite results. Their draw-punishment, Peer, black ritual and life-drain packages supply concrete inventories. Reid Duke's2012 Pox article supplies the established Pox/Smallpox/Liliana/Hymn attrition lineage. Adding Sorin, shared-life Bloodletter/Pox conversion and Oloro support is original2HG engineering. Do not claim that Sheoldred Pox is a tournament-proven winning cEDH archetype.

G2: Albert's12/25 registration is explicitly a casual-labelled event; Jeff Flynn's20/31 cEDH-labelled entry went0-4. They are actual source lists, not strong performance evidence. Mitrian's published Oloro primer supports enchantment, lifegain and alternate-win identity. Mesa Enchantress, enchantment copies, Rector, Replenish, Test and an independent Blood payoff package make this an Esper enchantment-control deck, not green Enchantress translated illegally. Lower-powered creature payloads in source lists became efficient counters and card selection.

H1: Pedro Vidaurri and Ty Ohio have actual first-place registrations in38- and35-player events. Their Tymna/Malcolm compact-win/interaction packages are the strongest source pedigree in this batch. The budget removes ubiquitous expensive mana/tutors and preserves Force/Oracle/Consultation plus evasive Pirates. Acererak is a new cross-team role, not a card attributed to either source list.

H2: David Freijo's5/22 and Duncan McClellan's6/22 Chulane lists both actually contain Aluren. Dork acceleration, Curio/Drake, Alarm/Earthcraft and creature toolbox packages are retained in spirit and exact-card comparisons. Black Cavern Harpy and Acererak are illegal in Bant and absent from H2; Acererak instead belongs to H1. Stefan Stasiak's primary Legacy interview informs the complementary value/combo architecture without claiming his Legacy results for Chulane.

I1: Jason Scott's1/18 and Toni Romero's2/44 Gitrog registrations provide complementary Dakmor/tutor and Loam/Depths land-recursion inventories. These are actual event facts. Keep Dakmor/discard, Loam/recursion and compact threat packages; omit banned Primeval Titan. The specified Woodland/Analyst route provides a deterministic mana benchmark without asserting that random dredge triggers can always be shortcut to a win.

I2: Mark Domzil's1/59 and Philip Jorzik's1/21 Shorikai registrations supply a genuine legal Azorius artifact-control commander pedigree. Both are source registrations, not Stoneblade2HG results. Reto S.'s primary Stoneblade submission supplies Stoneforge/Batterskull/Kaldra with cantrips/counters; its page displays76 total cards and is not silently accepted as a valid60-card tournament list. The newly designed Shorikai Stoneblade hybrid keeps those defining threats, adds Pilot equipment carriers and removes source stax that hurts Gitrog.

# Organizer review — urgent unresolved questions

1. **Aluren2 + Acererak0 across H2/H1 is functional.** Both commanders can be absent; Lost Mine Dark Pool loops drain both opponents. Keep it in the adversarial benchmark. Recommend reviewing Aluren's individual price; no new pairing surcharge or prohibition was applied.
2. **Bloodletter0 + Pox0 can kill a60-life enemy team while its caster's team survives.** Pox also destroys friendly resources. Sorin5 + Bloodletter0 is another sudden conversion. G1's free Sheoldred command zone and G2's free Oloro command zone remain inherited prices, not a new human endorsement.
3. **Test7 and Felidar5 begin above their win thresholds at60.** Their upkeep timing and interaction windows are actual constraints. Rector0, Replenish0 and low-cost enchantment tutors improve access/recovery. G2 Test plan conflicts with careless Pox.
4. **Gitrog1 / Shorikai0 / Chulane0 command access remains very cheap.** Gitrog's Woodland loop is setup-heavy but deterministic in the specified state. Original raw Dakmor engine alone is not certified as an instant deterministic win.
5. **Symmetric locks can be friendly fire.** G Contamination and Pox may create oppressive play patterns. Their presence in a deck does not approve them for league play. No blanket turn-seven, infinite-combo or land-denial prohibition has been imposed.
6. Malakir Rebirth0 is an unreviewed flexible MDFC. Adding1 currently takes G1 to50 and G team121; a disclosed replacement with Undying Malice0 restores120 but loses the land face. Do not silently reprice it.
7. Every source result is ordinary Commander or explicitly casual-labelled. No paired2HG outcomes, simulation win rates, average wins/turns or achieved optimality proofs exist. These are aggressively built candidates, not a proof that every budget allocation has been exhaustively optimized.
8. Latest consolidated overrides are accepted working calibration. Some are exact numeric decisions, others fixed range choices; this batch does not activate either. Historical qualitative tiers and earlier decks remain unchanged.

The initial construction and tests ran in memory while the filesystem was read-only. Once write access was restored, the frozen package was saved, all56 Batch1/2/3 tests passed from disk, and all46 generated artifacts reproduced byte-for-byte. Publication uses the existing Git branch; no league rule or price is activated. Source snapshots and pinned Oracle were already local; the full Oct21 Oracle bulk refresh was not claimed. Official rules/ban pages were checkedOct21.

Acererak's Lost Mine line is finite-library constrained:119 casts and29 mandatory draws before thirty Dark Pools. The early-game example has sufficient library; no indefinite draw-bypass shortcut is assumed.

Woodland loop colored-mana accounting uses Woodland, three Forests and one Swamp. Each iteration yields7G+2B, spends7G+B and banksB;32B really pays Exsanguinate X30. A five-green-land proof would produce green mana and would not by itself pay the spell'sBB.

# Conditional turn demonstrations

Read opening_examples.json for exact own-player seven-card hands, optional additional draws and sequenced costs. These are existence examples, not measured goldfish frequencies. No mulligan simulation or paired game was run.

- G1 can deploy Bloodletter onT2 with Ritual and cast Pox onT3. Both players still face interaction and friendly resource loss. G2 must choose between keeping protection up for this and casting its own Test onT3.
- G2's ordinary3-land/Signet Test line wins onT4 upkeep if>=50 twice. It is invalid if G1 Pox has reduced the pool below50.
- H2 can resolve Aluren onT3 from3lands and mana dorks; H1's own Acererak then supplies a complete repeated-dungeon win. Its own protection resources are specified separately.
- H2 can alternatively deploy Chulane onT3, Aluren onT4 and draw through Drake. Lab Maniac timing is explicitly checked before the library empties.
- I1's illustratedT3 Gitrog/Imp/Dakmor is an engine deployment, not a claimedT3 deterministic kill. A separate fixed-state Woodland/Analyst proof avoids unknown library order.
- I2'sT4 Basalt/Rings requires a fourth land drawn byT4 in addition to its opening7. Starting mana for the first copy activation is explicitly counted.

For mulligans, prefer colored development plus an engine or genuine interaction. Do not keep a nominal two-land hand merely because the total includes colorless utility lands. Coordinate keeps but never transfer cards or mana. Starting team skips its first draw step; none of the7-card-only demonstrations quietly assumes aT1draw.

# Commander Doubles Batch3 — season0-proposed

Read organizer_audio_review.md first, then teams.csv, decks/, score_ledger.csv, rules_interactions.md and organizer_review_and_limits.md. G/H/I are six complete independent100-card decks; H1 has two legal Partners and98 main cards. No rules or price activation and no experimental unbans.

## Reproduce from repository root

~~~sh
python commander-doubles-deck-benchmarks/build_batch3.py
python commander-doubles-deck-benchmarks/build_batch3.py --check
python -m unittest discover -s commander-doubles-deck-benchmarks/tests -p test_batch3.py -v
python commander-doubles-deck-benchmarks/score_batch3.py commander-doubles-deck-benchmarks/batch3/decks/G1.txt --deck-b commander-doubles-deck-benchmarks/batch3/decks/G2.json --summary
~~~

Uses the existing Python dependencies, pinned Oracle and source snapshots; ordinary scoring is offline. Frozen inputs are deck_inputs.json, review_content.json, research/foundations.json and source_checks.json. Latest price authority is the accepted_working_price_overrides_2026-10-21.csv file committed at0b1d2dd. Copy is frozen under research for deterministic historical regeneration.

price_snapshot.csv is sparse: every known legal card with any nonzero actual-zone price is present. All other verified legal paper Oracle identities in the hashed archive are zero; unknown names remain errors. Separate zone prices replace rather than add. README and price manifest identify the exact override composition.

Sources are attributed factual registrations already in the authorized archive. No mass scrape, paid API, inaccessible primer reproduction or invented standings. New deck changes are original analysis. The current linkedCR and official banned list were rereadOct21; pinned Oracle snapshot remainsOct20, not a claimed new bulk download. Text lists have Commander/Deck sections; JSON uses submitted_deck with Oracle IDs and version/checksum metadata.

Earlier Batch1/2 lists and retotal files are preserved. Source results do not belong to these adaptations. All budget checks use120 team/72 head/60 reference/12 max transfer and zero synergy surcharge.

rules.caution: No normal equip/Aid onto I1 Gitrog or Marit Lage. Shared blocking reduces simple combat clocks. Shorikai is an artifact until crewed.

rules.state: I2 owns Scepter imprinted with Reversal and nonland mana sources producing>2 per round.
rules.operation: Own Basalt3 plus Signet/Fellwar can accumulate mana. Reversal untaps only I2 nonlands; Ballista converts own mana, Shorikai can draw bounded cards.
rules.caution: I1 resources cannot pay I2 costs. Do not draw past own library. Artifact hate stops the engine.

rules.state: I2 owns both and can seed first untap3 plus copy2.
rules.operation: Copy Basalt untap; after copy resolves tap for3 before original resolves; after original resolves tap for3 again. Six produced per5 spent; Ballista X60 costs120 and shoots60.
rules.caution: Rings does not copy an ally's ability. Demonstrate seed mana; Basalt has no ordinary untap.

rules.state: Compare Shorikai source stax with I1 graveyard/dork plan.
rules.operation: RIP, Cage, Totem and Humility were omitted because they attack I1 engines. Lantern can instead target an enemy grave card or exile only opponents' graveyards.
rules.caution: Lantern ETB can target any graveyard: choose carefully. No broad assertion that all graveyard hate is teammate-safe.

rules.state: Friendly head targets one enemy with Chant/Abeyance while teammate acts.
rules.operation: Chant stops that enemy's spells; Abeyance stops its instants/sorceries and nonmana activated abilities. Barracuda stops enemies casting on its controller's friendly shared turn.
rules.caution: Other enemy and already-stacked objects remain. Barracuda costs4 and is not made free by Aluren.

rules.state: Use shared-team turns and separate resources.
rules.operation: Sorin ultimate controlling a player controls that player's team for that turn. Skip-draw would skip friendly team's whole draw step. Extra turns would be extra team turns.
rules.caution: Necropotence is absent from all six. No blanket infinite-combo/early-win prohibition or unban activated.
